newsitem.title: USA: US seminary student to plead guilty to gun charges.
newsitem.headline: US seminary student to plead guilty to gun charges.

text.p: A seminary student who tried to board a commercial flight at Tampa airport carrying an arsenal of weapons stuffed in a duffle bag will plead guilty to firearms and explosives charges, the U.S. attorney's office said on Wednesday.
Roman Christian Regman, 21, has been in custody since Sept. 2 when he was arrested carrying guns and explosives onto a flight bound for Pennsylvania. He was indicted on Sept. 10.

Assistant U.S. Attorney David Rhodes told Reuters Regman said on Tuesday he wanted to change his plea to guilty to four counts of possession of unregistered firearms and explosives. Two other charges will be dropped.
"They will schedule a rearraignment and a sentencing will be set up down the road sometime," Rhodes said. "He still faces a substantial maximum sentence," he added.

Regman is a seminary student at St. Tikhon in Pennsylvania, part of the Orthodox Church. Police said when he was arrested he was carrying a 9 mm pistol, two hand grenades, other explosive devices and bomb-making equipment, six military knives, several hundred rounds of ammunition, a ski mask and gloves.
A later search of his apartment in Brooksville, Florida, about 60 miles (100 km) north of Tampa, yielded an AK-47 assault rifle, a silencer and other explosives.
Rhodes said a motive for Regman's actions had not yet been established. His mother has denied he is a terrorist.
